title: How JPL keeps the 13-year-old Curiosity rover doing science
summary: This IEEE Spectrum article reveals how NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory has kept the Curiosity rover operational on Mars for 13 years, far exceeding its original 2-year mission design, through innovative engineering solutions, careful resource management, and creative problem-solving to overcome aging hardware challenges.
problem_solved: Extending the operational life of a robotic space rover far beyond its design specifications while continuing to conduct meaningful scientific research on Mars.
why_valuable: Demonstrates remarkable engineering resilience and provides rare insights into the practical challenges of maintaining robotic systems in extreme interplanetary environments for over a decade.
